Source. `STRING_SWITCH_L(p)` case-folds the witness bytes at offsets 32719..32722, so the malformed line beginning `if-M` still matches the `If-M` header family. The `HEADER("If-Modified-Since")` macro then rechecks `: ` at offsets 32736..32737 and materializes `raw.value = data_copy + 32738` and `raw.len = 17` from the short value bytes `Mon,\x9c18 Oct 27777`.

Root cause. The only admission check is `raw.len != 0`, so the short 17-byte source value from step 3 is still treated as parseable. The fix changes this to an exact 29-byte length check for the RFC1123 form `Wed, 17 Apr 2019 13:59:27 GMT`.

Because step 5 allows the short header, the caller passes only `raw.value` into `lwan_parse_rfc_time()`. The separate `raw.len` is dropped, so the callee receives a bare pointer even though its parameter type `const char in[static 30]` assumes a full RFC time string plus terminator.

Inside `lwan_parse_rfc_time()`, the first `STRING_SWITCH(str)` accepts `Mon,`; the blind `str += 5` at line 65 skips byte `0x9c` at offset 32742, `parse_2_digit_num()` then accepts `18 `, the month switch accepts `Oct `, and `parse_int(strndupa(str, 4), -1)` uses the first four year bytes `2777`. After the later line-95 `str += 5`, `str` has advanced from `raw.value = data_copy + 32738` to `data_copy + 32755`, which is the NUL written by step 4 over the original `\r`.

At `data_copy + 32755` the hour parse fails immediately on the inserted NUL, but line 98 still executes `str += 3`, moving `str` to `data_copy + 32758` where the later `:` from trailing bytes `oN:` makes the minute parse fail. Lines 100 and 102 likewise keep incrementing after failure, so `str` advances to `data_copy + 32761` and then `data_copy + 32764` inside the zero-filled tail left beyond `length`.
